incident-bot: [INCIDENT] metering.alert: ratecap failover on token-aggregator-usw2. Severity=P2. Symptoms: token counting drift + delayed emits -> possible false overage flags. Pager: @Maya. Runbook: <https://runbooks.internal/redwood/metering-ratecap-failover>
Maya (oncall-sre): On it. I'm seeing lots of fallback-to-slow-path logs around 17:48 UTC, backlog building in emitter queue.
Jin (metrics): Quick sample from real-time query: SELECT sum(tokens) FROM emitter WHERE window='1m' GROUP BY service -> last_min: expected 45k, observed 8k, backlog ~37k. Spike started ~1718087900. :eyes:
Raj (billing-ops): We're already getting overage flags for ~120 customers (mostly small). Likely false positives from late-emitted tokens. Can we pause alerts while we triage?
Irene (support): Support has 2 tickets and one SOC escalated email. Customers asking why they got an overage email — please hold alerts if possible.
Tom (infra): Possible root: ratecap controller detected a hot shard and moved traffic to fallback path which disables KV-prefix caching. That inflated per-token cost and slowed emits. I'll check controller logs.
Maya (oncall-sre): Mitigation plan (quick): 1) Pause customer-facing overage alerts via feature-flag (safe window). 2) Increase ratecap threshold on token-aggregator for 10m to allow catch-up. 3) Kick off backfill job to emit pending tokens. 4) Monitor billing-counter reconciliation and cancel false flags.
Eve (eng): How do we pause alerts? Which flag?
Maya (oncall-sre): Use alert-snooze service: 
```bash
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/v1/flags/overage-alerts/snooze" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"duration":600, "reason":"ratecap-failover - triage"}'
```
Maya (oncall-sre): Tom, can you raise ratecap threshold on aggregator (us-west-2) for 10m and enable temporary bypass for KV-cache on the fallback path so we don't lose prefix caching? I won't make lasting config changes without infra sign-off.
Tom (infra): Applying a staged config now: rolling update to aggregator-service -> bump ratecap 2x, enable cache-bypass-disabled flag on fallback (so fallback still uses cache). Rolling to 50% first.
Jin (metrics): New metrics coming in; emitter backlog decreasing from 37k -> 12k in 3min after partial rollout. token-emit-latency down from 4.2s -> 1.1s.
Raj (billing-ops): I'm going to run a quick recon job to map overage flags -> emit timestamps and mark ones likely false-positive. If alerts are snoozed, we can bulk-cancel notifications.
Irene (support): I'll update the customer-facing template: "We're investigating an anomaly that may have caused incorrect overage notifications. We're pausing alerts and will follow up." Sending to support channel.
Maya (oncall-sre): Backfill job started: backfill-emitter --start 1718087800 --end 1718088400 --priority=high
Eve (eng): Noted a related trace: token-aggregator pod OOM killed at 17:46, autoscaler added new pods but they hit cold-cache — explains slowdown.
Maya (oncall-sre): Current status: alerts snoozed, partial config rolled, backfill running, backlog trending down. Next: full rollout if stable for 5m, then re-enable alerts and reconcile billing counts.
Raj (billing-ops): I'll take handoff for billing reconciliation and customer refunds if we see confirmed false overages. Assigning postmortem to Tom + Maya.
Tom (infra): Will collect controller logs and config diff. Planning postmortem soon.
Maya (oncall-sre): Handoff to Raj and Support for customer comms. If anything regresses ping @Maya. Closing pager if metrics stay stable for 10m. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Pager closed by Maya at 1718088420 (duration 6m20s). Incident state -> mitigated. Postmortem: https://postmortems.internal/redwood/1718088080-ratecap-failover
